pr.title: Match a passkey registration on websites and usernames
pr.head: fcc9eae63f6c3d439c6858ce7b03a90c980b72d6

summary: The passkeys plan describes a small Mac and iPhone app whose AutoFill extension creates and signs with passkeys stored in multipass. When a site registers a new passkey, the extension must decide which store entry gets it. This pull request changes only that decision, in the plan's text; no code exists yet, and the plan stays draft.

Before this change, the extension picked an entry by name alone: the entry named after the site's relying party ID (the domain a passkey belongs to, such as github.com), or a numbered variant. That went wrong in two ways. A password entry with a different name, such as github work, got a second, passkey-only github.com entry beside it. And an entry holding one account's password could take a different account's passkey, mixing two accounts in one entry.

1. The same account registering again still replaces its passkey in place, matched by relying party ID and user handle.
  2. An existing entry of the site's now takes the passkey when it holds no passkey, has no username or the registering account's, and belongs to the site, by its name or by a website line that matches https://<rp id> under the websites plan's website::matches. A matching username wins a tie, then name order.
  3. Otherwise a new entry is created under the first unused name of <rp id>, <rp id> <user name>, <rp id> <user name> 2, and so on, with the account's user name as its username.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Relying party ID: the domain a passkey is registered for, such as github.com. A page on login.github.com may use it.
  • User handle: the site's opaque ID for the account, which identifies the same account registering again.
  • User name: the readable account name the site sends, such as octocat.
  • website::matches(stored, page): the websites plan's one matching function. Here the stored side is the entry's website line and the page is https://<rp id>.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The first review of this head requested changes, with two findings open: the tie order, and the unstated dependency on the websites plan. Its five suggestions ask for clarifications in § 2.1, § 2.2, § 4, and § 6.

groups.title: Choosing a registration's entry
groups.kicker: The passkeys plan's registration rule, and the sections that restate it
intro: The change rewrites § 2.1 step 5 as three rules tried in order, then brings the rest of the plan into line: § 2.2 says a passkey never joins another account's entry, § 2.5's src/ffi.rs row lets the extension find a site's entries by name and by website, § 4 adds one acceptance row per new case, and § 6 questions 7 and 8 record the owner's decisions.

Joining an entry only adds a passkey field, so the entry's password, username, notes, one-time password, and history stay as they were. A passkey is replaced only for the same relying party ID and user handle.

checks.text: With https://<rp id> as the page, a stored https://github.com matches the relying party IDs github.com and login.github.com, but a stored https://login.github.com does not match github.com. A tenant such as alice.github.io never matches evil.github.io.

files.note: The passkeys plan: § 2.1 step 5's three rules, and the matching edits to § 2.2, § 2.5, § 4, and § 6.

checks.text: Open finding: when github.com and github work (with website https://github.com) both have no username and no passkey, name order picks github work, because a space sorts before ., while § 6 question 7 says the entry named github.com gets the passkey.

Open finding: step 5 and this row need the websites plan's website lines and website::matches, but the plan never says it ships after the websites plan, which is scheduled next while this plan is now.
This row's outcome holds only when the github.com entry's username is octocat. An entry with no username would take the passkey under step 5's second rule.

Question 8's "an entry of that name exists that the account cannot join" agrees with step 5's "that no entry uses": the second rule already takes any joinable entry of that name, so the third rule adds at most one entry per registration. Checked by walking the three rules over the § 4 cases.
